The definitions of the terms developed reserves, exploratory well, field, proved reserves, and undeveloped reserves have been abbreviated from the respective definitions under Rule 4-10(a) of Regulation S-X.  The entire definitions of those terms under Rule 4-10(a) of Regulation S-X can be located through the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) website at www.sec.gov.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Ad valorem tax.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A tax based on the value of real estate or personal property.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Bbl.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume, used in reference to oil, NGLs, water, or other liquid hydrocarbons.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">BBtu.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One billion British thermal units.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Bcf</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One billion cubic feet, used in reference to gas.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">4</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">BOE.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Barrels of oil equivalent.  Oil equivalents are determined using the ratio of six Mcf of gas to one Bbl of oil or NGLs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Btu.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">  One British thermal unit, the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a one-pound mass of water by one degree Fahrenheit.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Developed acreage.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;font-style:italic;">  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The number of acres that are allocated or assignable to productive wells or wells capable of production.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Developed reserves.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Reserves that can be expected to be recovered: (i) through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared to the cost of a new well; and (ii) through installed extraction equipment and infrastructure operational at the time of the reserves estimate if the extraction is by means not involving a well.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Development well.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Dry hole.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A well found to be incapable of producing either oil, gas, and/or NGLs in commercial quantities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Exploratory well.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">  A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or gas in another reservoir.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Fee properties.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The most extensive interest that can be owned in land, including surface and mineral (including oil and gas) rights.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Field.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on or related to the same individual geological structural feature and/or stratigraphic condition.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Formation.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A succession of sedimentary beds that were deposited under the same general geologic conditions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Gross acre.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">An acre in which a working interest is owned.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Gross well.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A well in which a working interest is owned.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Horizontal wells.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Wells that are drilled at angles greater than 70 degrees from vertical.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Lease operating expenses.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The expenses incurred in the lifting of oil, gas, and/or NGLs from a producing formation to the surface, constituting part of the current operating expenses of a working interest, and also including labor, superintendence, supplies, repairs, maintenance, allocated overhead costs, and other expenses incidental to production, but not including lease acquisition, drilling, or completion costs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MBbl.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One thousand barrels of oil, NGLs, water, or other liquid hydrocarbons.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MBOE.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One thousand barrels of oil equivalent.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Mcf.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One thousand cubic feet, used in reference to gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBbl.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One million barrels of oil, NGLs, water, or other liquid hydrocarbons.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBOE.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One million barrels of oil equivalent.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBtu.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One million British thermal units.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMcf.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">One million cubic feet, used in reference to gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Net acres or net wells. </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> Sum of our fractional working interests owned in gross acres or gross wells.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">NGLs.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The combination of ethane, propane, isobutane, normal butane, and natural gasoline that when removed from gas become liquid under various levels of higher pressure and lower temperature.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">NYMEX WTI.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">New York Mercantile Exchange West Texas Intermediate, a common industry benchmark price for oil.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">NYMEX Henry Hub</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  New York Mercantile Exchange Henry Hub, a common industry benchmark price for gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">OPIS</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  Oil Price Information Service, a common industry benchmark for NGL pricing at Mont Belvieu, Texas.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">5</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">PV-10 (Non-GAAP).  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">PV-10 is a non-GAAP measure.  The present value of estimated future revenue to be generated from the production of estimated net proved reserves, net of estimated production and future development costs, based on prices used in estimating the proved reserves and costs in effect as of the date indicated (unless such costs are subject to change pursuant to contractual provisions), without giving effect to non-property related expenses such as general and administrative expenses, debt service, future income tax expenses, or depreciation, depletion, and amortization, discounted using an annual discount rate of 10 percent.  While this measure does not include the effect of income taxes as it would in the use of the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows calculation, it does provide an indicative representation of the relative value of the Company on a comparative basis to other companies and from period to period.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Productive well.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A well that is producing oil, gas, and/or NGLs or that is capable of commercial production of those products.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved reserves.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Those quantities of oil, gas, and NGLs which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods, and government regulations prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation.  Existing economic conditions include prices and costs at which economic producibility from a reservoir is to be determined, and the price to be used is the average price during the 12-month period prior to the ending date of the period covered by the report, determined as an unweighted arithmetic average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each month within such period, unless prices are defined by contractual arrangements, excluding escalations based upon future conditions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Recompletion.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The completion of an existing wellbore in a formation other than that in which the well has previously been completed.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reserve life index.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Expressed in years, represents the estimated net proved reserves at a specified date divided by actual production for the preceding 12-month period.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reservoir.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil, gas, and/or associated liquid resources that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Resource play.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A term used to describe an accumulation of oil, gas, and/or associated liquid resources known to exist over a large areal expanse, which when compared to a conventional play typically has lower expected geological risk.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Royalty.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The amount or fee paid to the owner of mineral rights, expressed as a percentage or fraction of gross income from oil, gas, and NGLs produced and sold unencumbered by expenses relating to the drilling, completing, and operating of the affected well.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Royalty interest.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">An interest in an oil and gas property entitling the owner to shares of oil, gas, and NGL production free of costs of exploration, development, and production operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Seismic.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">sending of energy waves or sound waves into the earth and analyzing the wave reflections to infer the type, size, shape, and depth of subsurface rock formations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Shale.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Fine-grained sedimentary rock composed mostly of consolidated clay or mud.  Shale is the most frequently occurring sedimentary rock.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The discounted future net cash flows related to estimated proved reserves based on prices used in estimating the reserves, year end costs, and statutory tax rates, at a 10 percent annual discount rate.  The information for this calculation is included in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Supplemental Oil and Gas Information (unaudited)</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> located in Part II, Item 8 of this report.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Track record.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">  Current year conversions of proved undeveloped reserves to proved developed reserves, divided by beginning of the year proved undeveloped reserves.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Undeveloped acreage.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Lease acreage on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production of commercial quantities of oil, gas, and NGLs regardless of whether such acreage contains estimated net proved reserves.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Undeveloped reserves.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage, or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion.  The applicable SEC definition of undeveloped reserves provides that undrilled locations can be classified as having undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless the specific circumstances justify a longer time.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Working interest.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The operating interest that gives the owner the right to drill, produce, and conduct operating activities on the property and to share in the production, sales, and costs.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">6</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s1AA8F65303805DB89CB6BE51553F92D2"></a></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:center;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">PART I</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">When we use the terms &#8220;SM Energy,&#8221; the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; or &#8220;our,&#8221; we are referring to SM Energy Company and its subsidiaries unless the context otherwise requires.  We have included certain technical terms important to an understanding of our business in the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Glossary of Oil and Gas Terms</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> section of this report.  Throughout this document we make statements and projections that address future expectations, possibilities, or events, all of which may be classified as &#8220;forward-looking.&#8221;  Please refer to the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Cautionary Information about Forward-Looking Statements</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> section of this report for an explanation of these types of statements and the associated risks and uncertainties.</span></div><div><a id="sEF7562EE693150368F14D78C590C5F06"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEMS 1. AND 2.  BUSINESS AND PROPERTIES</span></div><div><a id="s9E6C06675B7A58E2938983AC007F7DC4"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">General</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We are an independent energy company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, development, and production of oil, gas, and NGLs in the state of Texas.  SM Energy was founded in 1908, incorporated in Delaware in 1915, and our initial public offering of common stock was in December 1992.  Our common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol &#8220;SM.&#8221;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our principal office is located at 1775 Sherman Street, Suite 1200, Denver, Colorado 80203, and our telephone number is (303) 861-8140.</span></div><div><a id="s0230CF37971154CAA721D83F876A89DB"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Strategy</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">At SM Energy, our purpose is to make people&#8217;s lives better by responsibly producing energy supplies, contributing to domestic energy security and prosperity, and having a positive impact in the communities where we live and work.  Our long-term vision for the Company is to sustainably grow value for all of our stakeholders.  We believe that in order to accomplish this vision, we must be a premier operator of top tier assets.  Our current energy project development portfolio is focused on oil and gas producing properties in the state of Texas.</span></div><div><a id="s308450874FDF5C94A9876669DF002C2A"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Significant Developments in 2019</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Strategic Transformation.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">During 2019, we completed our strategic transformation, which commenced in 2016 through a series of asset acquisitions and divestitures.  For the fourth quarter of 2019, we passed an important milestone by achieving a positive difference between our net cash provided by operating activities and our net cash used in investing activities.  Our operational execution in 2019 was outstanding, achieving our objectives in important industry metrics, including key top-quartile benchmarks for environmental, health, and safety performance.  We were also successful in proving up additional investment opportunities on our existing acreage positions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Production.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">  Our average daily production in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> consisted of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">59.9</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MBbl of oil, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">300.8</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMcf of gas, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">22.2</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MBbl of NGLs, for an average net daily equivalent production rate of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">132.3</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;MBOE, which represented a </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">10 percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> compared with </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  This </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> was primarily driven by a </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">25 percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">increase</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in production volumes from our Midland Basin assets as a result of strong well performance, increased drilling and completion efficiencies, improved completion designs, and longer laterals.  We completed more lateral feet in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> compared with </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, driving continued increases in volumes at a lower average drilling and completion cost. Please refer to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Areas of Operation</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">below for additional discussion.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves and Capital Investment.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our estimated proved reserves </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">decreased</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">eight percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">462.0</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">503.4</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. However, the impact of lower commodity prices in 2019 was offset by a net derivative cash settlement gain of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$39.2 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for the year ended </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, compared to a net derivative cash settlement loss of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$135.8 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. Our total capital program in 2020, is budgeted to be between $825.0 million and $850.0 million, and is expected to be approximately 20% lower compared with 2019, in large part due to significant cost reductions and efficiencies that were achieved in 2019.  Our 2020 program will be focused on highly economic oil development projects in both our Midland Basin and South Texas assets.  We expect total production volumes in 2020 to decrease slightly compared with 2019 as expected continued growth in our oil production volumes will not completely offset expected decreases in gas and NGL production volumes.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Sustainability is a key focus of our plans, in terms of positioning ourselves financially to participate in future energy investment opportunities, and executing our strategy of being a premier operator with high standards for corporate responsibility. As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, there were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">51</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> gross (</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">48</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> net) wells that had been drilled but not completed in our Midland Basin program.  Estimated proved reserves increased </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">nine percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">234.1</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at year end </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">214.3</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at year end </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  This increase was driven by additions of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">58.9</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE from discoveries, extensions and infill, and acquisitions, partially offset by </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">12.6</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of downward revisions from price, performance, and aged proved undeveloped reserves.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">South Texas.</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">  Our South Texas assets are comprised of approximately 158,900 net acres located in Dimmit and Webb Counties, Texas (&#8220;South Texas&#8221;).  Our current operations in South Texas are focused on developing the Eagle Ford shale formation and delineating the Austin Chalk formation.  Our overlapping acreage position in the Eagle Ford shale and Austin Chalk formations covers a significant portion of the western Eagle Ford shale and Maverick Basin Austin Chalk (&#8220;Eagle Ford shale&#8221;) and includes acreage across the oil, gas-condensate, and dry gas windows with gas composition amenable to processing for NGL extraction.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we incurred </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$160.9 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of costs and averaged </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">one</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> drilling rig and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">one</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> completion crew.  We completed </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">31</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> gross (</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">20</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> net) wells during </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and full-year regional production </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">increased</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">one percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> year-over-year to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">22.0</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE for </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, there were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">21</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> gross (</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">21</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> net) wells that had been drilled but not completed in our South Texas program.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Certain drilling and completion activities in the northern portion of our South Texas acreage position were primarily funded by a third party pursuant to our joint development agreement.  The agreement provided that the third party carried substantially all drilling and completion costs and receives a majority of the working and revenue interest in these wells until certain payout thresholds are reached.  This arrangement allowed us to leverage third-party capital to prove up the value of our Eagle Ford North area, while also allowing us to test cutting edge technology, capture additional technical data, satisfy certain lease obligations, and potentially expand economic drilling inventory in the future.  All wells subject to this agreement were drilled and completed as of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">During 2019, we added </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">43.0</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of estimated proved reserves, offset by downward revisions of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">82.1</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE, of which </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">68.5</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE resulted from decreased commodity pricing and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">10.3</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE resulted from performance revisions.  As a result, estimated proved reserves </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">decreased</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">21 percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">227.8</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at year end </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">289.1</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE at year end </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div><a id="sE52836F662765F67A39D72EC2E787EC6"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Reserves</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Reserve estimates are inherently imprecise and estimates for new discoveries and undeveloped locations are more imprecise than reserve estimates for producing oil and gas properties.  Accordingly, we expect these estimates to change as new information becomes available.  The following table presents the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows and pre-tax PV-10 (&#8220;PV-10&#8221;).  PV-10 is a non-GAAP financial measure, and generally differs from the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, because it does not include the effects of income taxes on future net revenues.  Neither the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows nor PV-10 represents the fair market value of our oil and gas properties.  We and others in the oil and gas industry use PV-10 as a measure to compare the relative size and value of proved reserves held without regard to the specific tax characteristics of such entities.  Please refer to the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Glossary of Oil and Gas Terms</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> section of this report for additional information regarding these measures and refer to the reconciliation of the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows to PV-10 set forth below.  The actual quantities and present value of our estimated proved reserves may be more or less than we have estimated.  No estimates of our proved reserves have been filed with or included in reports to any federal authority or agency, other than the SEC, since the beginning of the last fiscal year. #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved Undeveloped Reserves</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Proved undeveloped reserves include those reserves that are expected to be recovered from future wells on undrilled acreage, or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion.  Undeveloped reserves may be classified as proved reserves on undrilled acreage directly offsetting development areas that are reasonably certain of production when drilled or where reliable technology provides reasonable certainty of economic producibility.  Undrilled locations may be classified as having proved undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless specific circumstances justify a longer time.  As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we did not have any proved undeveloped reserves that had been on our books in excess of five years, and none of our proved undeveloped reserves were on acreage expected to expire or on acreage that was not expected to be held through renewal before the targeted completion date.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">For proved undeveloped locations that are more than one development spacing area from developed producing locations, we utilized reliable geologic and engineering technology when booking estimated proved undeveloped reserves.  Of the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">214.9</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of total proved undeveloped reserves as of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">60.1</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of proved undeveloped reserves in the Midland Basin and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">68.7</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of proved undeveloped reserves in our South Texas position were offset by more than one development spacing area from the nearest developed producing location.  We incorporated public and proprietary data from multiple sources to establish geologic continuity of each formation and their producing properties.  This included seismic data and interpretations (3-D and micro seismic), open hole log information (both vertically and horizontally collected) and petrophysical analysis of that log data, mud logs, gas sample analysis, measurements of total organic content, thermal maturity, test production, fluid properties, and core data as well as statistical performance data yielding predictable and repeatable reserve estimates within certain analogous areas.  These locations were limited to only those areas where both established geologic consistency and sufficient statistical performance data could be demonstrated to provide reasonably certain results.  In all other areas, we restricted proved undeveloped locations to development spacing areas that are immediately adjacent to developed spacing areas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, estimated proved undeveloped reserves </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">decreased</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">43.7</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">17 percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> compared with </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. The majority of additions in our Midland Basin and South Texas programs resulted from future development projects identified by our on-going development and portfolio optimization activities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Removed for five-year rule.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As a result of our testing and delineation efforts in 2019, we revised certain aspects of our future development plans to focus on maximizing returns and the value of our assets.  As a result, we removed </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">9.8</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of estimated proved undeveloped reserves and reclassified these locations to unproved reserve categories.  The reclassified locations were generally replaced by locations with higher quality proved undeveloped reserves, which are reflected as additions from discoveries, extensions, and infill.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Conversions to proved developed.  </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> conversion rate was </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">26 percent</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  During </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we incurred </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$686.3 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> on projects with reserves booked as proved undeveloped at the end of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, of which </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$611.1 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> was spent on converting proved undeveloped reserves to proved developed reserves by </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.  At </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, drilled but not completed wells represented </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">26.8</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> MMBOE of total estimated proved undeveloped reserves.  We expect to incur </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$182.0 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of capital expenditures in completing these drilled but not completed wells, and we expect all estimated proved undeveloped reserves to be converted to proved developed reserves within five years from their initial booking as proved undeveloped reserves.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, estimated future development costs relating to our proved undeveloped reserves were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$591.5 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$615.6 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$458.1 million</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2020</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2021</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2022</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Internal Controls Over Proved Reserves Estimates</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our internal controls over the recording of proved reserves are structured to objectively and accurately estimate our reserve quantities and values in compliance with the SEC&#8217;s regulations.  Our process for managing and monitoring our proved reserves is delegated to our corporate reserves group and is coordinated by our Corporate Engineering Manager, subject to the oversight of our management and the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors, as discussed below.  Our Corporate Engineering Manager has approximately 12 years of experience in the energy industry and has been employed by the Company for 10 years.  He holds a Bachelor of Science Degree in Petroleum Engineering from Montana Tech of the University of Montana and is a Registered Professional Petroleum Engineer in the states of Texas, Wyoming and Montana.  He is also a member of the Society of Petroleum Engineers.  Technical, geological, and engineering reviews of our assets are performed throughout the year by our regional staff.  Data, obtained from these reviews, in conjunction with economic data and our ownership information, is used in making a determination of estimated proved reserve quantities.  Our regional engineering technical staff do not report directly to our Corporate Engineering Manager; they report to either their respective regional technical managers or directly to the regional manager.  This design is intended to promote objective and independent analysis within our regions in the proved reserves estimation process.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Third-party Reserves Audit</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Ryder Scott is an independent petroleum engineering consulting firm that has been providing petroleum engineering consulting services throughout the world for over 70 years.  Ryder Scott performed an independent audit using its own engineering assumptions, but with economic and ownership data we provided.  Ryder Scott audits a minimum of 80 percent of our total calculated proved reserve PV-10.  In the aggregate, the proved reserve amounts of our audited properties determined by Ryder Scott are required, per our policy, to be within 10 percent of our proved reserve amounts for the total Company, as well as for each respective region.  The technical person at Ryder Scott primarily responsible for overseeing our reserves audit is an Advising Senior Vice President who received a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from Purdue University in 1979 and a Master of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1981.  He is a licensed Professional Engineer in the State of Texas and a member of the Society of Petroleum Engineers and the Society of Petroleum Evaluation Engineers.  The </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> Ryder Scott report concerning our reserves is included as Exhibit 99.1.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In addition to a third-party audit, our reserves are reviewed by our management with the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors.  Our management, which includes our President and Chief Executive Officer, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, and Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, is responsible for reviewing and verifying that the estimate of proved reserves is reasonable, complete, and accurate.  The Audit Committee reviews a summary of the final reserves estimate in conjunction with Ryder Scott&#8217;s results and also meets with Ryder Scott representatives, apart from our management, from time to time to discuss processes and findings.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">12</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s64D7A25A38485318A32B69300ECD181D"></a></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Production</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The following table summarizes the volumes and realized prices of oil, gas, and NGLs produced and sold from properties in which we held an interest during the periods presented. style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">A productive well is an exploratory, development, or extension well that is producing or is capable of commercial production of oil, gas, and/or NGLs.  A non-productive well, frequently referred to within the industry as a dry hole, is an exploratory, development, or extension well that proves to be incapable of producing oil, gas, and/or NGLs in sufficient commercial quantities to justify completion, or upon completion, the economic operation of a well.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">As defined by the SEC, an exploratory well is a well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or gas in another reservoir.  A development well is a well drilled within the proved area of an oil or gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.  The number of wells drilled refers to the number of wells completed at any time during the respective year, regardless of when drilling was initiated.  Completion refers to the installation of equipment for production of oil, gas, and/or NGLs, or in the case of a dry hole, the reporting to the appropriate authority that the well has been abandoned.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In addition to the wells drilled and completed in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> (included in the table above), we were actively participating in the drilling of 22 gross (20 net) wells and had 66 gross (63 net) drilled but not completed wells as of January 31, 2020.  These drilled but not completed wells represent wells that were being completed or were waiting on completion as of January 31, 2020.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">14</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s6B3B34DB038B5D109E6158B27DB067A7"></a></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Acreage</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The following table sets forth the number of gross and net surface acres of developed and undeveloped oil and gas leasehold, fee properties, and mineral servitudes that we held as of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.
